"PLEASE READ BEFORE ENTRUSTING YOUR PET HERE"

I am sharing my experience so that other pet parents can make informed decisions and hopefully avoid the pain and trauma I have gone through.

My dog, Lambhorgini, was admitted to this veterinary hospital on 17 December 2025 at approximately 11:00 PM. The veterinarian on duty insisted that he be admitted for “better treatment” and informed us that pet parents were not allowed to stay back in the hospital. Trusting the professional advice given, we agreed to the admission.

At the time of admission, he was placed on oxygen and, while I was present, appeared to be stabilizing and recovering. At no point was I informed that his condition was critical or that his life was at immediate risk.

The following morning, I was informed that he had passed away at an estimated time of 8:30 AM.

What has been most distressing is not only the sudden loss of my deeply loved pet, but the lack of communication, transparency, and responsibility throughout the process. Even post-event, no clear explanation or accountability was provided by the designated veterinarian on duty at the time.

As a pet parent from Singapore, I am extremely disappointed by the quality, efficiency, and professionalism experienced at this facility. Entrusting a beloved companion to a hospital should come with honest updates, proper communication, and accountability — all of which were lacking in this experience.

Based on what I went through, I would strongly advise other pet parents not to entrust their pets to this facility at any given time. Pets deserve competent care and responsible medical oversight, especially during critical situations.

I am sharing this review solely so that other pet parents can make an informed choice and do not experience the same heartbreak.

Sakeena Thakker , pet parent of Lambhorgini

I brought my cat to Andheri Vetic clinic at 4AM from Thane due to sudden breathing problems. The X-ray showed fluid in his lungs, which required urgent intervention.

I took my cat for grooming under anesthesia on June 8. No blood tests or pre-anesthesia screening were performed before the procedure. After anesthesia, my cat remained unconscious for nearly two days and was not eating, drinking, urinating, or defecating normally. Despite repeatedly sharing videos and concerns, we were told that his condition was normal.
When his condition worsened, further tests revealed fluid accumulation in his abdomen. We later consulted other veterinarians, who questioned why no blood tests had been done before anesthesia. Sadly, my cat passed away a few days later.
What made this even more heartbreaking was being offered compensation or another cat instead of receiving accountability. Pets are family members and cannot be replaced. I am sharing my experience so that other pet owners can make informed decisions.

featured_reviews.name: vikas nalawade
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review about a stray cat named “Leopard” who eventually became our family member. Request you to please read it till end, as it may be helpful to any pet parent.
Leopard met with an accident and was missing for a week’s period. Later we found him & we noticed that he had a fracture at shoulder of right forelimb. Doctors told us that leg needs to be operated by inserting rod in his leg, so we got him operated by Dr. Sunetra. The surgery went well, but three days after surgery, Leopard's operated leg started swelling, we informed Dr. Sunetra but she told us it is the swelling due to surgery and it will subside downwards. But that swelling was due to infection and it lead to pus formation. Next day the swelling increased and in the evening pus started oozing out, seeing this we called up Dr. Sunetra & rushed to her with our Leopard. Dr. told us to keep flushing the wound twice a day with betadine. After 2-3 days of this treatment, the skin around the infected area went dead and we had a clear sight of his wound with operated area, where we could see his bone from two points because healing was not completed & the stitches were opened. We even asked Dr. Sunetra the doubt in our mind that this infection will not spread in his operated leg & internal body, to which she responded, it would not.
Eventually his external pain reduced but he had internal pain, which we failed to understand. He could not tolerate the pain and stopped eating and got fever exactly on 8th day from operation. We informed this situation of Leopard at every visit to Dr. Sunetra, but she recommended to force feed our Leopard. Later on our Leopard left with no energy to walk on his own and lift his neck, he even started heavy breathing. After informing this situation to Dr. Sunetra, she then advised us to put saline for his recovery but nowhere had she conveyed that Leopard’s health is deteriorating & he needs hospitalization. At this time, she was going out of town & was not available for 4-5 days.
Since, Dr. Sunetra was not available, we went to other Vet doctor who knew Leopard's medical history. This doctor told us to continue saline treatment twice a day for at least 4-5 days. Here the blood test was also done to examine the condition of our Leopard, where the report came with alarming & critical output depicting WBC increased & Platelets dropped to severe condition. Even this doctor also not recommended that our Leopard require hospitalization. This was the 11th day after operation.
The 12th day story (i.e. 1st July 23) of our Leopard was worst. The morning session of his saline was completed & even this second doctor went out of town for 3-4 days without recommending hospitalization. By evening, somewhere from 4:30pm, the heavy breathing became worse & we could not see his pain. We started calling Dr. Sunetra, but her phone was not reachable, so we text her on WhatsApp along with Leopard’s blood report. Since no response from doctor, with Leopard, we rushed to a Vet hospital, where he was admitted with a note by the doctors, like heavy breathing & drop in body temperature, which was very critical condition. He was kept in ICU incubator with oxygen supply to ease his breathe & improve his body temperature. The hospital doctors even told us that there are chances that the infection might have spread into blood. Unfortunately battling with pain & breathing problem our Leopard passed away on the same day around 11 pm.
There are certain questions for Dr. Sunetra;
# Why you haven't included any medicine for infection post-surgery?
# Why you did not advised us prior to start saline, when we informed you that Leopard lost his appetite?
# Why you did not look closely if the infection was spreading in the body? If you think it wasn't then why did he lost his appetite, had weakness, got fever, started heavy breathing?
# Why you took everything so lightly and casually in his case? Was it because it was a stray cat?

The doctor’s entire focus was on the operated area and the wound & the rest health parameters were ignored completely.

featured_reviews.name: sms sweta
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a pet parent, I’m sure many of you will understand the kind of fear and helplessness we feel when something isn’t right with our baby. I went through exactly that when my 14-year-old feline, Goldie, was diagnosed with a serious tumour on her left paw. Those days were filled with worry, questions, and uncertainty.

All we knew was that we needed the right oncologist — someone we could trust completely. That’s when we found the incredible team at Superpets, and from that very first visit, everything began to feel a little lighter.

From explaining the diagnosis and possible causes, to guiding us through every test, every step was handled with so much patience, clarity, and compassion. What truly stood out was how reassuring the entire team was — always available to answer questions, clear doubts, and take that extra effort to make both us and Goldie feel comfortable.

The journey — from diagnosis, to surgery, to post-operative care and stitch removal — was smoother than we could have ever hoped for. Every decision they made felt right, thoughtful, and in Goldie’s best interest.

A special note of gratitude to Dr. Pratyush, Dr. Vasudha, and Dr. Gauri — you are truly angels in disguise. The care, dedication, and gentleness with which you handled Goldie means the world to us. It’s not just medical expertise, but your genuine love for animals that makes all the difference.

I must admit, I was initially skeptical about traveling all the way from the suburbs to Bandra for treatment — but today, I can say with complete conviction that every visit, every effort, was absolutely worth it.

What touched me deeply was that even after a month, Dr. Pratyush personally followed up to check on Goldie’s health. That level of care is rare and speaks volumes about the kind of people they are — not just doctors, but true lifesavers.

This entire experience has been a journey of gratitude. People like them are not just treating animals — they are healing families.

Thank you, Superpets team, from the bottom of my heart, for taking such beautiful care of our baby.

Forever grateful. 🙏🏻

They immediately took charge of the situation. He underwent operation and was discharged in 5 days. We had to take him for regular follow ups and on a follow up in a weeks time, doctors suspected something wrong and again on further tests discovered that his spleen had got affected and damaged along with few further conditions that had developed. He underwent second surgery. He battled for his life for a month in this hospital. He was hospitalised.
